the identification of nitric oxide‐producing vestibular pathways, with the aim of understanding the interplay between nitric oxide and classic neurotransmitter systems in vestibular function.

L‐citreulline is a marker of nitric oxide‐producing cells, that nitric oxide is produced in vestibular neurons, and that these neurons project into vestibulo‐autonomous and vestibulo‐motor pathways.

nitric oxide‐producing vestibular neurons are located in subregions of each of the four vestibular nuclei, and that the L‐citruline‐immunostaining method is a reliable and sensitive method for visualizing these neurons.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
nitric oxide‐producing neurons are present within the vestibular nuclear complex, and that these cells may be involved in vestibulo‐autonomous and vestibulo‐motor reflexes.
the vestibular system is a good candidate for the study of nitric oxide in the central nervous systems.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of L‐cetrulline in the vestibular nuclei of the brainstem is a good indicator of the presence of nitiric oxide.
nitric oxide‐producing cells can be identified in the vestibular nuclei by L‐citruline immunoreactivity.
